name: Saul and Doeg at Nob
charge: Slaughter of the priests of the Lord on an informer's report
summary: Doeg the Edomite, Saul's chief herdsman, told the king that Ahimelech had given David bread and Goliath's sword. Saul summoned the priests, condemned them unheard, and when his own guard refused to strike them, Doeg killed eighty-five men in linen ephods and then the whole city of Nob.
offense: Doeg reported to Saul that Ahimelech had received David at Nob, enquired for him, given him food, and supplied Goliath's sword (1 Samuel 22:9-10). Saul treated help given to David as conspiracy against himself. Ahimelech answered that David was the king's faithful servant and son in law and that he knew nothing of a plot (1 Samuel 22:11-15). His defence was heard but rejected. The king's suspicion had taken the place of a righteous judgment. Saul ordered the priests killed. His servants refused to stretch out their hands against the priests of the Lord, but Doeg obeyed, killing eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod. He then smote Nob, including its households and animals (1 Samuel 22:16-19). The refusal of the guard shows that the king's order did not remove the responsibility of those commanded. Doeg did what others would not do. Exodus 23:1 forbids joining a false report or becoming an unrighteous witness; verse 7 forbids slaying the innocent and righteous. Psalms 52 names the malicious tongue that loves evil rather than good. Speech and violence worked together at Nob: the report furnished an occasion, the king supplied the order, and the willing hand carried it through.
judgment: Psalms 52:5-7 pronounces the overthrow of the man who trusted in riches and strengthened himself in wickedness. He would be plucked from his dwelling and rooted out of the land of the living. His apparent strength was not a refuge from the God whose priests had been struck. The righteous would see and fear: the wealth and royal favour he trusted could not establish his house against the Lord.

entries.commentary: The priest gave David hallowed bread, for there was no bread there but the shewbread that was taken from before the Lord. Remember David had been out in the field three days, fearful of king Saul, when he came to Nob in need. Link this history with the words of Christ: when the Pharisees challenged his disciples for plucking the ears of corn on the sabbath day, Christ recounted this very history of David and the shewbread. Precept this in your bibles if you do not have it already.

David fled that day for fear of Saul and went to Achish the king of Gath, and the servants of Achish knew him by the song, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands. David laid up these words in his heart and was sore afraid of Achish, so he changed his behaviour and feigned himself mad, scrabbling on the doors of the gate and letting his spittle fall down upon his beard. David was playing crazy; he was fearful, and Achish dismissed him as a mad man.

Here you see that Saul had placed an Edomite over his servants: Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, answered and reported that David had come to Nob and that Ahimelech had inquired of the Lord for him, given him victuals, and given him the sword of Goliath the Philistine. The scriptures tell us we are never supposed to trust our enemies, yet what we are reading is Saul with an Edomite set over his servants.

Saul commanded his footmen to turn and slay the priests of the Lord, but the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the Lord. Saul was able to get the Edomite to do what his own men would not do: Doeg turned and fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod, and smote Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword. Go back to Genesis and see the spirit that has been placed on this man from the beginning: Esau comforted himself with the purpose of killing his brother Jacob. Just as in the time of Saul, even to this very day, when Israel suffers violence at the hands of the other nations, especially Esau, he gets comfort out of killing us; when Saul appointed Doeg to that task, you can best believe he was quite happy over it and most likely found much pleasure in killing the priests.

To the chief musician, Maschil, a Psalm of David, written when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul that David had come to the house of Ahimelech. Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? The man of sin has to be revealed, and our people still do not want to acknowledge that Esau is the devil, not Christ. The white picture of Jesus is a deception; the Bible says nothing like that. -
Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs, like a sharp razor, working deceitfully. -

Thou lovest evil more than good, and lying rather than to speak righteousness. You thought he loved black people; he loves evil, and lying rather than righteousness. So-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans are a reminder of how the Most High really looks and that Esau sold his birthright.
Thou lovest all devouring words, O thou deceitful tongue.

God shall likewise destroy thee for ever; he shall take thee away and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living. There will be no white people in the kingdom; there will be a period of slavery, and then they die and it is over.
The righteous also shall see, and fear, and shall laugh at him. -
Lo, this is the man that made not God his strength, but trusted in the abundance of his riches, and strengthened himself in his wickedness. He trusted in his slave trades and his riches. -
But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God; I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever. -
I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it; and I will wait on thy name, for it is good before thy saints. -

Thou shalt not raise a false report, nor put thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness: basically, thou shalt not lie. If you did not see it, do not make up a story like you were there; keep your mouth shut. Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

Neither shalt thou countenance a poor man in his cause. This deals with judgment: do not be a respecter of persons because a man is poor, as if he is automatically wrong when he brings a matter against a rich man. The judges were charged to hear the small as well as the great. In this corrupt system in Babylon, how innocent or guilty you come out depends on how much lawyer you can afford. Our law was holy and righteous because none of that made a difference: either you were right or you were wrong, whether poor or rich. The Pharisees learned the ways of the heathen and began respecting persons, which the book of James speaks against.

If thou meet thine enemy's ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again; if thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, thou shalt surely help with him. This enemy that hates you is your brother, your own nation, not the other nations as [Matthew 5:44](/bible/matthew/5#v44) is misconstrued to mean. [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) proves it, saying the same law with thy brother in the place of thine enemy: thou shalt not see thy brother's ox or sheep go astray; in any case, no matter how you feel, bring them again unto thy brother. And if thou know him not, keep it in thine own house until thy brother seek after it. He is still your brother even if you never grew up with him; that is real love for your own people. Deuteronomy means the second law; it speaks the law plain in case you did not understand it here. Keep [Deuteronomy 22:1-4](/bible/deuteronomy/22#v1) and [Leviticus 19:17-18](/bible/leviticus/19#v17) in your hip pocket with this verse.

Thou shalt not wrest the judgment of thy poor in his cause: verse six explains verse three again in case you did not catch it, do not be partial in judgment. Keep thee far from a false matter; the innocent and righteous slay thou not, for the Most High will not justify the wicked. Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous: do not take a bribe when it comes to judgment; be upright and honest.

Also thou shalt not oppress a stranger, for ye know the heart of a stranger, seeing ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. This is speaking about us, as [Exodus 22:21](/bible/exodus/22#v21) already laid out with [Leviticus 25:35](/bible/leviticus/25#v35).

Six years thou shalt sow thy land, but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still, that the poor of thy people may eat, and the beasts of the field after them; likewise the vineyard and the oliveyard. That is mercy from the Lord: in the seventh year the land itself fed the poor. The seventh year ties into the count of the jubilee: seven sabbaths of years to the forty-ninth year, and in the fiftieth year no plowing of the land, which the law takes up later.

Six days do thy work, and on the seventh day rest, that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid and the stranger may be refreshed. The stranger here can be another nation working for you: they too get their due rest on the sabbath. When the Lord sets Israel back up to rule, the nations will kick and scream at first, but once these laws are applied there will be righteousness reigning over the earth like they have never seen, and all will be refreshed on the sabbath, spiritually and physically.

Make no mention of the name of other gods is not saying you cannot pronounce the names Buddha, Allah, Krishna, Ra. Christ himself named Beelzebub, the chief of the devils, a name derived from the Philistine god of Ekron, and Christ did no sin; so the verse cannot mean the bare saying of a name. The Lord says this same thing three ways in this one chapter, and the other two places show the meaning: verse 24, thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works; and verses 32 and 33, thou shalt make no covenant with them nor with their gods, for if thou serve their gods it will surely be a snare unto thee. Make no mention means do not learn how to serve and worship them. Joshua and Deuteronomy double it: neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them; and if thy brother or son or wife entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, thou shalt not consent. Wherever you are, do not go trying to find out how the nations worship their gods.

Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year: all the males appeared before the Lord God three times in the year. The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover, kept in the time appointed of the month Abib, the first month of the year, as it is written, the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover. None shall appear before me empty: you could not come empty-handed. You brought the tenth of your oil, your wine, whatever was required, for the priests to replenish the storehouses. The feast of harvest, the firstfruits of thy labours, is also known as Pentecost and the feast of weeks; and the feast of ingathering, in the end of the year, is also known as the feast of tabernacles and the feast of booths.

Thou shalt not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, neither shall the fat of my sacrifice remain until the morning. The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk: the Lord repeats what was read at [Exodus 22:30](/bible/exodus/22#v30), that the young one was not to be taken too young and too soon; it stayed its seven days with his dam before it was given.

Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, obey his voice, provoke him not, for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him. That Angel is speaking of Christ. If thou indeed obey his voice, I will be an enemy unto thine enemies and an adversary unto thine adversaries. These enemies are not the same enemy of verse four: the enemy of verse four is your brother whom you must help and shew mercy; these enemies in verse 22 the Lord himself deals with and destroys for you.

The Angel goes before Israel unto the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, to cut them off. Thou shalt not bow down to their gods nor serve them nor do after their works, but utterly overthrow them and quite break down their images. Serve the Lord your God, and he shall bless thy bread and thy water, take sickness away from the midst of thee, none casting their young nor barren in the land, and the number of thy days he will fulfil. He drives the nations out by little and little, lest the land become desolate and the beasts multiply, until Israel be increased and inherit the land. The bounds are set from the Red Sea even unto the sea of the Philistines, and from the desert unto the river, the river Euphrates. That little sliver on the map today is not how big Israel is supposed to be: the land was to encompass all the way out to the Euphrates by Babylon, taking in parts of what is Iraq and Iran, and it will be filled one day.

Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods. They shall not dwell in thy land, lest they make thee sin against me: for if thou serve their gods, it will surely be a snare unto thee. This is the third way the Lord states the command of verse 13 in this chapter: no learning their worship, no serving, no covenant.

verses.text: Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the Lord; and his name was Doeg, an Edomite, the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul.
Then answered Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, and said, I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
And he enquired of the Lord for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.

And Saul said unto him, Why have ye conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse, in that thou hast given him bread, and a sword, and hast enquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, And who is so faithful among all thy servants as David, which is the king’s son in law, and goeth at thy bidding, and is honourable in thine house?

Did I then begin to enquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute any thing unto his servant, nor to all the house of my father: for thy servant knew nothing of all this, less or more.
And the king said, Thou shalt surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all thy father’s house.

And the king said unto the footmen that stood about him, Turn, and slay the priests of the Lord; because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not shew it to me. But the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the Lord.

And the king said to Doeg, Turn thou, and fall upon the priests. And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod.
And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen, and asses, and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.
And Abiathar shewed David that Saul had slain the Lord’s priests.
And David said unto Abiathar, I knew it that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul: I have occasioned the death of all the persons of thy father’s house.
Abide thou with me, fear not: for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life: but with me thou shalt be in safeguard.
Why boastest thou thyself in mischief, O mighty man? the goodness of God endureth continually.
Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs; like a sharp razor, working deceitfully.
Thou lovest evil more than good; and lying rather than to speak righteousness. Selah.
Thou lovest all devouring words, O thou deceitful tongue.
God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living. Selah.
Keep thee far from a false matter; and the innocent and righteous slay thou not: for I will not justify the wicked.

lawsResolved.text: Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
Government officers that engage in conspiracy, treachery and murder are to be put to death.
If a ruler hearken to lies, all his aides and ministers become wicked.
You shall not go about speaking slander or spreading false reports about others.
Doing injustice by justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous is an abomination and condemned by God.
